label: input g at positions 4-6 in sequences that start with r
explanation: Sparse conjunctive feature. Its context is clear: about 90% of activation mass is in sequences whose first token is r, at steps t=4-6 (original phase, plus the <DEL> step when L is 4-6). It never fires in the copy phase or at t<3. Within that context, the strongest trigger is the input g (52% of mass, 14x lift), especially when g directly follows one of n/w/v/h/u. The top activations are all r ... n g or r ... w/v/h g. It also fires weakly on other tokens that follow n/w/v/h/u in r-initial sequences, and on <DEL> when the next output is r. The predicate (first=r, input g, t=4-6) has dev F1 0.25 and mass recall 0.40. The broad context (first=r, t=4-6) gets 87% mass recall but only 2% precision, so most r-initial position 4-6 steps do not activate. Magnitude is highest for g right after n/w/v/h (about 0.7-1.0 of max). Requiring the preceding letter raises precision to about 0.5 but cuts recall to about 0.11.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=r (+7.08), prev_tok=n (+4.69), orig1=d (+3.68), prev2_tok=n (+2.90), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=g (+2.75), phase=0 & in_tok=g (+2.75). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.94), phase=2 (-3.78), prev3_tok=r (-2.25), prev3_tok=- (-2.15).
